jobs.title: Launch Operator-Alabama
jobs.description:
WindBorne Systems is supercharging weather forecasts with a unique proprietary data source: a global constellation of next-generation smart weather balloons targeting the most critical atmospheric data. We design, manufacture, and operate our own balloons, using the data they collect to generate otherwise unattainable weather intelligence.

Our mission is to eliminate weather uncertainty, and in the process help humanity adapt to climate change, be that predicting hurricanes or speeding the adoption of renewables. We are building a future in which the planet is instrumented by thousands of our microballoons, eliminating gaps in our understanding of the planet and giving people and businesses the information they need to make critical decisions. The founding team of Stanford engineers was named Forbes 2019 30 under 30 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Khosla Ventures and Footwork VC.

We are hiring a part-time balloon launch operator to support our weather forecasting mission. You'll be launching high-altitude weather balloons that collect atmospheric data used to improve forecasts for events like hurricanes and wildfires. The role is hands-on and outdoors, with shifts on weekends, evenings, and occasional weekdays.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Launch high-altitude weather balloons following established safety and operational procedures

 - Meet weekly launch targets to support WindBorne's data collection and forecasting goals

 - Set up and break down launch sites, ensuring equipment is properly configured and secured

 - Manage and maintain inventory of balloon supplies, compressed gas cylinders, and related equipment

 - Perform routine equipment checks and flag any maintenance or safety concerns

 - Adapt to varying weather conditions and outdoor environments during operations
   
    


SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

 - Follows detailed processes and safety procedures with precision

 - Clear and timely communicator

 - Comfortable with computers and hands-on technical equipment

 - Experience with compressed gas cylinders a plus, but not required

 - Thrives in outdoor environments and enjoys working as part of a team




BENEFITS

$25-28 per hour. We are considering a range of backgrounds and experience levels for this position and adjust our offers accordingly to be competitive with market rates.




LOCATION

Bay Minette, Alabama and surrounding area. In-person required.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI & Automation
jobs.description:
At NerdWallet, we're building tools and experiences that help people make smarter financial decisions. As a Software Engineer focused on AI & Automation within our Security organization, you'll build production software and AI-enabled systems that make security work more scalable, effective, and developer-friendly across NerdWallet.

 

You'll apply strong software engineering fundamentals and hands-on AI experience to automate complex security workflows, build internal platforms and developer tooling, and help us rethink how security engineering operates in an AI-native environment. You do not need to come from a traditional security engineering background. We're looking for an engineer who has built and operated production software and AI-enabled systems, is curious about security, and is excited to develop deeper security expertise while solving meaningful problems at scale.

 

You'll have room to bring new ideas, influence how AI and automation practices evolve at NerdWallet, and shape a growing area within Security. This role reports to the Security Automation Manager.




PROJECTS YOU MAY BE WORKING ON IN THIS POSITION INCLUDE:

 - Designing and building AI-enabled workflows and multi-agent systems that automate security design review, threat modeling, policy Q&A, vulnerability analysis, and other high-value security processes.

 - Building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and semantic search experiences across large code and documentation repositories.

 - Creating automated code-review capabilities that help identify insecure patterns and improve software quality earlier in the development lifecycle.

 - Building production Python services and APIs that power AI-enabled security workflows, with thoughtful architecture, authentication, authorization, testing, observability, and reliability.

 - Designing and operating scalable pipelines that ingest, process, index, and retrieve large volumes of code, documents, and events.

 - Improving AI system quality through evaluation frameworks, experiment management, prompt and context management, observability, and evidence-based iteration.

 - Managing practical production tradeoffs such as latency, reliability, model/provider selection, token usage, and cost.

 - Designing integrations with GitHub, Slack, Jira, Confluence, LLM providers, and internal services so security guidance fits naturally into engineering workflows.

 - Applying security controls to AI applications, including prompt injection defenses, sensitive-data handling, access control, supply-chain considerations, and safe model inputs and outputs.

 - Identifying new opportunities for software, automation, and AI augmentation across the Security team and independently moving high-value ideas from problem definition through production.


WHERE YOU CAN MAKE AN IMPACT:

 - Own technically meaningful software and AI initiatives from problem definition through production and ongoing operation.

 - Help shape how AI and automation are used across NerdWallet Security, including when AI is the right solution and when it is not.

 - Build tools and platforms that make security easier for engineering teams to adopt and use.

 - Improve the speed, consistency, and quality of security workflows through thoughtful software design and automation.

 - Grow into deeper application and AI security expertise while bringing strong software engineering judgment to the team.

 - Communicate technical tradeoffs clearly and collaborate with engineers, security partners, and non-technical stakeholders.


YOUR EXPERIENCE:

 - 3+ years of professional software engineering experience building and operating production software.

 - Strong Python proficiency, including hands-on experience building production backend services and APIs.

 - Experience designing maintainable backend architectures, including separation of concerns, request/response validation, authentication/authorization, error handling, testing, and observability.

 - Experience developing distributed or cloud-based systems and making practical decisions about scalability, reliability, and performance.

 - Hands-on experience building production AI-enabled applications or automations using LLM APIs, agents/tool use, RAG/retrieval, or comparable architectures.

 - Experience defining, evaluating, and improving the quality of AI-enabled systems in production.

 - Ability to work through ambiguity, identify opportunities independently, and move technical work from idea to implementation.

 - Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical decisions, tradeoffs, and limitations clearly.

 - Interest in secure software development and willingness to build deeper expertise in application security and AI security.


WHERE:

 - This role will be remote (based in the U.S.).

 - We believe great work can be done anywhere. No matter where you are based, NerdWallet offers benefits and perks to support the physical, financial, and emotional well being of you and your family.




WHAT WE OFFER:

Work Hard, Stay Balanced (Life’s a series of balancing acts, eh?)

 - Industry-leading medical, dental, and vision health care plans for employees and their dependents

 - Rejuvenation Policy – Flexible Vacation Time Off + 11 holidays + holiday company shutdown

 - New Parent Leave for employees with a newborn child or a child placed with them for adoption or foster care

 - Mental health support

 - Paid sabbatical after 5 years for Nerds to recharge, gain knowledge, and pursue their interests

 - Health and Dependent Care FSA and HSA Plan with monthly NerdWallet contribution

Have Some Fun! (Nerds are fun, too)

 - Company-wide events like NerdLove (employee appreciation) and our annual Charity Auction

Plan for your future (And when you retire on your island, remember the little people)

jobs.title: Failure Analysis Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

With electric vehicles expected to be nearly 30% of new vehicle sales by 2025 and more than 50% by 2040, electric mobility is becoming a reality. ChargePoint (NYSE: CHPT) is at the center of this revolution, powering one of the world’s leading EV charging networks and a comprehensive set of hardware, software and mobile solutions for every charging need across North America and Europe. We bring together drivers, businesses, automakers, policymakers, utilities and other stakeholders to make e-mobility a global reality.

Since our founding in 2007, ChargePoint has focused solely on making the transition to electric easy for businesses, fleets and drivers. ChargePoint offers a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to create an all-electric future and a trillion-dollar market.

At ChargePoint, we foster a positive and productive work environment by committing to live our values of Be Courageous, Charge Together, Love our Customers, Operate with Openness, and Relentlessly Pursue Awesome. These values guide how we show up every day, align, and work together to build a brighter future for all of us.

Join the team that is building the EV charging industry and make your mark on how people and goods will get everywhere they need to go, in any context, for generations to come.

Reports To

Sr. Manager - Product Quality and Failure Analysis Engineering (PQE/FAE)

What You Will Be Doing

ChargePoint is looking for a Failure Analysis Engineer with an interest in hands-on failure analysis lab of electronics and PCBA including AC/DC converters, DC/DC converters, electrical components, and modules. In this role, you will lead failure analysis investigations, interpret findings from electrical and physical testing, and communicate root cause conclusions to cross-functional teams. You will own investigations end-to-end—from initial fault isolation through final corrective action—ensuring exceptional quality at every stage of ChargePoint’s electric vehicle charging products. To be successful at ChargePoint this person must be highly motivated, self-directed, and comfortable working in a loosely structured and fast-paced environment. Training and mentorship will be provided for candidates who bring strong analytical foundations and a willingness to learn hands-on electrical and physical analysis techniques.

What You Will Bring to ChargePoint

As a Failure Analysis Engineer, your responsibilities will focus on conducting and interpreting root cause analysis:

• Lead system- and component-level failure analysis for customer field returns, new product introductions, and factory yield excursions; identify patterns across multiple failure events to surface systemic issues

• Performs laboratory hands-on electrical and physical failure analysis for fault isolation on electronic products (EVSE, AC/DC converters, DC/DC converters, PCBA, and cable harness); interprets test data and documents findings in formal failure analysis reports

• Defines and executes test plans for functional electrical testing, circuit analysis, fault isolation, probing, and failure duplication; communicates root cause conclusions to engineering and cross-functional stakeholders

• Collaborates with engineering and operations teams to identify the root cause for issues related to field, manufacturing, supplier quality, and product design

• Drives corrective and preventive action (CAPA) closure; maintains KPIs and databases; engages directly with suppliers or contract manufacturers on quality escapes as needed

• Drives ambiguous problems to resolution independently, translating incomplete or conflicting data into clear findings and actionable next steps.

Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Mechatronics, or a related technical field with 0–2 years of experience (new graduates welcome). Relevant coursework, capstone projects, and internships count toward experience.

• Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics and component data sheets

• Familiarity with electrical systems and components (PCBA, MOSFETs, IGBTs, Capacitors, Relays, Cable Harness, etc.) including their failure modes/mechanisms

• Familiarity with or exposure to electrical test equipment such as Digital Multi-meter (DMM), Oscilloscopes, Power Supplies, Electronic Loads, etc.

• Familiarity with physical failure analysis techniques such as optical microscopy and 2D / 3D X-ray

• Experience applying problem solving tools including Root Cause Analysis

• Ability to work independently as a self-starter; comfortable driving investigations with limited guidance and adapting approach as new data emerges

• Interest in electronics industry such as automotive, consumer electronics, solar, electric vehicle, AI data centre, or battery

• Willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to 10% of the time

Location

Campbell, CA

The base salary range for this role is $83K – $112K per year. In addition, this position is eligible for annual merit-based RSU grants. The company offers a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance; 401(k); paid time off; parental leave; life and disability insurance; and wellness resources.

Compensation may be adjusted based on work location.

jobs.title: Flight Control Operator
jobs.description:
Are you someone who: 

 - Enjoys building deep expertise in complex systems 

 - Thrives without a reliable script to follow 

 - Is interested in building real-world-applicable intuitions for wind patterns and forecasts 

Then you might be a good fit for WindBorne’s Flight Control Operator role! 

WindBorne Systems operates the world's largest constellation of autonomous weather balloons. We achieve full atmospheric coverage by launching balloons spread across time and space, but sometimes need to navigate them to specific locations—like into the eye of a typhoon. Balloons navigate by changing their altitude: drop ballast to ascend, or vent gas to descend. Different altitudes have different wind speeds and directions, so if you understand the wind field, you can route a balloon anywhere in the world. In practice, flight control is a mix of meteorology, physics, and operational judgment. 

The role: 

You'll become an expert at flying our balloons. We're not looking for someone to just follow procedures, we want you to get better at this than we currently are. Balloons fail often – sometimes from hardware issues, sometimes from weather, sometimes from our own mistakes. We launch a lot of them and we're constantly learning. You'll be developing new techniques and adapting as our hardware and software evolve. 

This isn't like driving a car, with predictable inputs and outputs. Commands take time to execute, forecasts have uncertainty, and every balloon behaves a bit differently depending on its current state and hardware. You'll develop specialized knowledge that lets you make good calls quickly – when to avoid vs head through rough weather, how to correct for forecast uncertainties, and how to reach locations that push the bounds of what our hardware is capable of. 

What we're looking for: 

 - Ability to learn independently in an environment where procedures are constantly evolving 

 - Comfort prioritizing and making judgment calls in high-pressure, uncertain environments

 - Excellent communication skills (oral and written), as well as the ability to collaborate effectively with engineering teams 

 - Willingness to work long or unusual hours to get the balloons where they need to go 

There’s no one set background that makes a great FC. Our current FCs have a wide range of past lives, from bike mechanics and wilderness guides to kpop academy learning managers. Above all, we’re looking for people who will genuinely love the day-to-day of learning to master flight control. If you think that’s you, we want to hear from you! 

Hours 

This is a part-time, fully remote position at approximately 20 hours per week, with an hourly rate of $24-$28 USD/hr. Hours are regularly scheduled rather than on-call — we'll work with you to find a consistent schedule that fits both your availability and our coverage needs. Weekend availability is strongly preferred. Reliable internet is required. 

This role is a good fit for U.S. citizens living abroad or anyone looking for steady part-time work with non-traditional hours. Please include your general availability (days/times and timezone) when you apply. 

Eligibility 

Due to the nature of our work supporting U.S. defense operations, this position requires U.S. citizenship. A security clearance is not required.

jobs.title: Lead GTM Engineer
jobs.description:
Look around you today, every store, home, hospital, school, was made possible by the coordination of architects and a team of professionals. They are charged with the responsibility of creating our shelters and yet, they are left with nothing more than Excel to manage their work. We're here to change that.

What is Monograph?

Monograph is a firm performance management platform for architecture and engineering practices. Firms use Monograph to make quick and confident decisions about budgeting and resources to drive their practices forward.

Why Work at Monograph?

People first: Core to the team, we believe in people first, curiosity, and empathy. You'll be a culture ambassador and deploy your genuine value for relationships to drive success and happiness.

Build a company that will redefine architecture: Project management is just the beginning...we have big ambitions to help facilitate the entire design process from becoming the document source of truth to coordinating with consultants. You can shape the future of building design.

Work with some of the best product people in the world: We’re an innovative team of highly productive individual contributors with a strong design background. You will be doing some of the best work of your life.

Build the systems that help Monograph and Total Synergy identify, convert, and retain customers.

Location: Remote

The opportunity

Monograph and Total Synergy have prospect and customer data spread across many systems. This role will connect that data, reduce manual work, and build automated workflows that improve how we acquire, convert, and retain customers.

How we define GTM Engineering

We are looking for someone who understands how revenue teams work and can personally build the systems they need. You will identify revenue problems, test practical solutions, and measure the results.

• Commercial first. Diagnose the revenue problem before selecting a tool or designing a workflow.

• Build to learn. Test ideas quickly and invest further only when they show value.

• Own outcomes. Judge each project by the revenue, customer, or productivity outcome it improves.

What you will own

1. Identify and prioritize GTM problems

• Work with Marketing, Sales, RevOps, and CX to follow the customer journey from first interaction through renewal and identify missed leads, slow handoffs, lost data, and repetitive manual work.

• Prioritize GTM engineering projects based on revenue impact, benefit to the GTM team, effort, and risk.

2. Connect and improve GTM data

• Connect data across Salesforce, HubSpot, Clay, Gong, websites, product, support, and billing systems using integrations, APIs, and automation tools.

• Build workflows that clean, enrich, deduplicate, match, and sync lead, opportunity, and customer data across systems.

• Work with RevOps and system owners to standardize data fields, permissions, lifecycle rules, and integrations.

3. Improve scoring and prioritization

• Use first- and third-party data to identify high-fit prospects, deals at risk, and customers likely to churn or expand.

• Improve how leads are scored and prioritized, and how contacts are categorized and matched to accounts.

• Use AI for research, summarization, classification, and personalization when it produces a better result than standard automation.

4. Build and maintain reliable workflows

• Build and test new workflows using automation tools, AI-assisted development, SQL, and lightweight code.

• Test workflows with real users and data before launch, including permissions, edge cases, and failure scenarios.

• Own workflows from launch through monitoring, maintenance, and retirement.

5. Measure results and drive adoption

• Document current performance and define a clear success metric before launching each workflow, then track adoption and business results after launch.

• Use testing and performance data to improve, scale, or stop workflows.

• Train users, gather feedback, and document the process so successful workflows become part of day-to-day work.

Examples of the problems you may solve

Prospect identification and conversion

• Build a scoring system that combines company fit and engagement signals, then directs each prospect to SDR, BDR, or continued marketing follow-up.

• Identify high-fit A&E firms showing signs of active demand, find the likely buyers, and coordinate Marketing and Sales outreach.

• Create a reliable account and contact view across Monograph and Total Synergy by resolving incomplete, duplicate, and conflicting records.

Seller productivity and pipeline progression

• Use call transcripts and account activity to identify deal risks, missing stakeholders, competitor mentions, and recommended next steps.

• Re-engage closed-lost or inactive opportunities when changes in company activity, engagement, or product needs create a new opening.

• Automate account research, CRM updates, meeting preparation, and follow-up while measuring the effect on conversion and sales-cycle speed.

Customer retention and expansion

• Build customer health models using onboarding, product adoption, support, billing, and engagement data to identify churn risk before renewal.

• Identify expansion opportunities based on product usage, company growth, additional offices, and previous customer conversations.

• Turn customer calls, support conversations, and product feedback into recurring insights for CX, Sales, Marketing, and Product.

How you will partner with existing teams

• VP Marketing: Sets the role’s priorities and ensures its work supports company-wide GTM goals.

• Revenue Operations: Manages the CRM, lifecycle stages, lead routing, forecasting, and official revenue reporting. You build workflows in partnership with RevOps.

• Marketing Operations. Manages campaign execution, marketing automation, and attribution. You build workflows that connect marketing systems with Sales and CX.

• Marketing, Sales, BDR, and Customer Experience: They define how they work with prospects and customers. You build and maintain the systems that support those processes.

• Product, Engineering, Data, and Security: They set standards for product data, infrastructure, security, privacy, and production integrations. You involve them when a workflow touches those areas.

How success will be measured

• Deliver measurable improvements in conversion, pipeline, deal progression, retention, or expansion.

• Reduce manual work and enable faster follow-up on high-priority prospects and customers.

What you bring

You understand how B2B revenue teams work and can turn a business problem into a reliable production workflow. You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical teams and focus on measurable commercial outcomes.

• 4+ years in GTM Engineering, RevOps, Marketing Ops, Growth Engineering, business systems, data automation, or a related field, with examples of systems you personally built.

• Strong knowledge of B2B SaaS funnels, CRM, marketing automation, lead and account management, sales workflows, and customer retention.

• Hands-on experience designing multi-system workflows with platforms such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Clay, n8n, Make, Zapier, Workato, or comparable tools.

• Working fluency with APIs, webhooks, JSON, SQL, data transformation, and AI-assisted scripting in Python, JavaScript, or a similar language.

• Experience using LLMs or AI agents for GTM workflows, with controls for quality, privacy, errors, and human review.

• Ability to define requirements, explain tradeoffs, and work across technical and nontechnical teams.

• A track record of measuring adoption and business impact, not just shipping automations or implementing tools.

Helpful, but not required

• Experience in vertical SaaS, ideally architecture and engineering software.

You'll Love Our Benefits

🎭 Innovative engineering and product culture

💰 Early-stage well-funded company

❤️ Inclusion and diversity as a company priority

And for US-based, full-time employees:

🌡 100% premium coverage on our healthcare plans for employees and their families

jobs.description:
At Accenture Federal Services, nothing matters more than helping the US federal government make the nation stronger and safer and life better for people. Our 13,000+ people are united in a shared purpose to pursue the limitless potential of technology and ingenuity for clients across defense, national security, public safety, civilian, and military health organizations.

Job Description:

As an Infrastructure Engineer in this role, you will be responsible for architecting and maintaining scalable, resilient systems that support high-volume data alerting within a dynamic, fast-paced environment. You will leverage your expertise in Kubernetes to orchestrate containerized workloads, ensuring seamless deployment and management of applications.

Success in this position will be driven by your hands-on experience with messaging platforms like RabbitMQ and Kafka, which are essential for handling large-scale data streams and ensuring reliable communication between services. You will benefit from familiarity with monitoring and observability tools such as Grafana, as well as logging and alerting frameworks that enable proactive incident response. Exposure to DevOps methodologies will be crucial, as you will collaborate closely with development teams to streamline CI/CD pipelines and enhance operational efficiency. Your ability to troubleshoot complex issues and implement best practices in cloud security and automation will set you apart in this challenging and rewarding role.

Here's what you'll do:

• Optimize cloud infrastructure on AWS, utilize services such as EKS, EC2, and S3, and implement infrastructure as code with Terraform to automate provisioning and configuration.

• Design robust routing and DNS solutions to guarantee high availability and performance across distributed systems.

Here is what you need:

• 8+ years of experience in DevOps or a similar field.

• Experience in several of the following areas: Kubernetes RabbitMQ Kafka EKS AWS Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) S3 Terraform Routing DNS Grafana Logging Alerting

Bonus points if you have:

• Experience with scalable applications on Kubernetes.

• Experience handling high volume data alerts.

• Experience working on large projects in complex, fast-paced environments.

• Active TS/SCI with Poly security clearance is required.

jobs.title: Systems Administrator II
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

ActBlue is a nonprofit organization dedicated to creating cutting-edge technology that fuels Democratic victories and enables progressive causes to thrive.

Our vision is simple: building change through the power of people. Since our founding, we’ve been building innovative solutions to revolutionize grassroots fundraising – if you’ve donated to a Democratic campaign or a progressive organization online, you’ve probably used our platform! We believe in putting power in the hands of small-dollar donors by helping thousands of groups — from local candidates to national movements — mobilize their communities and create a lasting impact. Every member of our team is deeply committed to advancing our shared mission and core values. Together, we are shaping the future of democracy.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Systems Administrator II will design, implement, and continually improve ActBlue’s internal IT systems, ensuring they meet the needs of a wide variety of stakeholders and stay aligned with evolving compliance, operational, and industry standards. In this role, you will help uphold data protection practices, manage access and identity infrastructure, and contribute to technical decisions that shape the day-to-day experience of a distributed team.

This position requires a strong technical foundation and a growing understanding of how system architecture connects to organizational compliance needs — including SOC 2, GDPR, and CCPA. You will identify and help reduce risk across systems, build and implement automation, and help embed data privacy and security into how ActBlue manages information and operations.

This role reports to the Sr. IT Manager and is part of the Systems Administration team, partnering closely with our Desktop Support team and collaborating cross-departmentally to deliver solutions that support the broader goals of the organization.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Configure, deploy, and manage secure, cloud-based IT systems — with a focus on identity management, MDM, endpoint security, and SaaS integrations

• Partner with Security, Legal, and Data Governance stakeholders to ensure IT systems meet regulatory requirements, internal controls, and proper security configurations

• Manage user identity lifecycle and access control, including implementation of RBAC, least privilege principles, and regular access audits

• Develop and implement technical controls for data governance, including data classification, data retention, data loss prevention, and secure data handling procedures

• Create and maintain systems documentation, playbooks, and user-facing knowledge resources to support IT operations and cross-functional alignment

• Design and implement IT process automation (e.g., onboarding/offboarding, software provisioning, and compliance checklists)

• Support internal audits and evidence gathering for compliance reporting, including review of logs, change management records, and security controls

• Stay current on evolving regulatory, privacy, and security standards to ensure systems remain aligned with industry best practices

• Contribute to IT project delivery in partnership with cross-functional teams, including project planning, vendor coordination, and implementation

WHAT YOU BRING

• 3+ years of experience in systems administration, with experience developing and implementing compliance- and security-driven projects

• Working knowledge of identity and access management platforms, MDM tools, and core productivity/collaboration suites, along with experience applying endpoint hardening and security configuration best practices

• Strong familiarity with macOS environments, including enforcing security policies, maintaining governance standards, and managing patch compliance across a device fleet

• Experience integrating SaaS tools and platforms, including planning and executing system and data migrations

• Exposure to workflow automation and orchestration tools, as well as emerging agentic or AI-driven tools that streamline IT operations

• Experience implementing data governance controls and operationalizing data privacy standards. Also familiar with relevant compliance frameworks (e.g., SOC 1 & 2, NIST, PCI DSS), as well as e-discovery and data handling policies and procedures

• Diligent and intentful in day-to-day work, with strong attention to detail and follow-through

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills — especially in technical documentation, policy writing, and cross-functional collaboration

• A proactive, collaborative mindset and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment

• Commitment to equity, accessibility, and a people-first approach to systems design and support

WORK & BENEFITS SNAPSHOT

This posting is for a full-time, remote, salaried position. Travel may be required to attend all-staff, departmental retreats, or select meetings. Additional travel may be required for select positions.

Registered States*:

Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington D.C.

*While ActBlue is currently registered to support remote work in the states listed above, we possess the ability to register in additional states as needed. If you are located in a state not listed, we may still be able to proceed with your application, but please note that the offer process may take longer to accommodate registration requirements.

Work Schedule:

This role requires availability during established, regular business hours (Mon-Fri) and potentially could be expected to be a part of an on-call rotation which will result in working nontraditional hours as needed.

Work Environment:

Employees can expect to work with distributed teams across all U.S. time zones. Our roles require extended technology usage, and proficiency with virtual communication tools such as Zoom and Slack. Regular attendance in virtual meetings is inherent to every position.

Salary Range Details:

Salary Range: $65,658 - $81,543 - $97,428

ActBlue is committed to consistent compensation practices across our organization. Final salary offers will take into account factors such as candidate experience, interview performance and current team salary parity.

Benefits:

• Flexible work schedules and an unlimited time-off policy

• Fully paid and trans-inclusive health, dental, and vision insurance for employees and their families; plus fully-paid health reimbursement arrangement to use for out of pocket expenses and fully-paid short- and long-term disability

• Fully paid basic and AD&D life insurance and a voluntary supplemental life insurance option

• Dependent and health care flexible spending account options

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP) benefits for employees

• Automatic 2% Employer-paid 401K contribution, plus up to an additional 6% match on employee contributions

• A minimum of three months paid medical, family and parental leave (for all new parents, adoptions included)

• Commuter or home-office benefits, including a $1,000 home-office setup allowance for all new full-time remote employees

• Additional perks including quarterly snack deliveries and digital subscriptions to the Boston Globe & New York Times

ActBlue is unable to sponsor work visas at this time.

UNION INFORMATION

The terms and conditions of this position are subject to a collective bargaining Communication Workers of America (CWA), Local 1400.

BACKGROUND CHECKS

As part of our hiring process, ActBlue will conduct a background check at the time of offer. This will be completed in compliance with applicable laws and will not be initiated without your consent.

INCLUSION STATEMENT FROM ACTBLUE

ActBlue is committed to equal employment opportunities and fostering a diverse, inclusive workplace. We celebrate unique perspectives, honor the dignity of all individuals, and recognize that diverse backgrounds and identities strengthen our mission.

If you’re passionate about our work and see yourself in this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you don’t meet every requirement.

We also provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities throughout the hiring process and employment. To request an accommodation, email recruitment@actblue.com.

*ActBlue will never ask candidates to buy equipment, nor will we email from anything other than an actblue.com or actbluetech.com email address.

AECOM's environmental practice is dedicated to helping industries, clients and governments meet their environmental responsibilities while protecting the natural environment. • Strong technical capability across hydrogeological conceptualisation, drilling supervision, aquifer testing, groundwater monitoring, mine dewatering, water supply and regulatory approvals.
• Experience managing projects or technical workstreams, including coordinating field programs, budgets, schedules and project deliverables.
• Demonstrated ability to prepare high-quality technical reports and proposals, interpret complex environmental and geoscientific datasets
• Ability to work independently, collaborate across multidisciplinary teams and provide technical guidance or mentoring to less experienced team members.

jobs.title: Donor Organizing - Program Associate
jobs.location: Hudson Valley or New York City
jobs.description:
North Star Fund is hiring a Donor Organizing Program Associate. We’re seeking a highly-organized person committed to community building across class and race.

The Donor Organizing Program Associate will help donors deepen their political education, strengthen their giving practices and stay connected to grassroots movements in New York. The Program Associate supports the design and coordination of programming that ensures that our donor community has meaningful, continuous opportunities to learn, take action and grow in relationship with North Star Fund.

This team member will grow and nurture North Star Fund’s network of people committed to transformative action through giving. This role requires collaboration across our internal teams. This is not a fundraising position. It’s a role focused on supporting dynamic programming for North Star Fund’s highly-engaged donor community.

Programming will support donors in developing giving practices that are

• values-driven

• aligned with the priorities and needs of grassroots movements

North Star Fund is a social justice fund. We support grassroots organizing led by communities of color building power in New York City and the Hudson Valley. We organize people across race and class to give in support of social justice movements. We also offer year-round programming to help organizers build and sustain their work.

North Star Fund was founded over 45 years ago by a group of New Yorkers who wanted to disrupt traditional philanthropic practices. They built the fund to be a collective giving community where donors support social justice movements. And they built it to support a different way to practice philanthropy. This means shifting power and resources to community organizers who make grantmaking decisions. North Star Fund began with a small handful of donors. Since then, thousands of donors have moved many millions through our grant programs.

This position is full-time. The Program Associate will report to the Donor Organizing Director and will regularly partner with other staff.

Primary Responsibilities

• Work in close coordination with North Star Fund’s Development and Grantmaking teams to create public programming. This programming will reflect the strategic priorities of these teams while amplifying our mission.

• Support the program development process for workshops aligned with North Star Fund’s mission. Workshops will support donors with how to be a stronger ally through one’s giving.

• Coordinate logistics for workshops, trainings and webinars. Communicate with participants, prepare documents, arrange food, take notes, and set up Zoom links.

• Share feedback and insights from donors and program participants with relevant teams. This will help improve and inform future programing and support provision.

• Track and manage data pertaining to program participants. Maintain and improve our relevant data systems.

• Draft clear, engaging content about North Star Fund’s donor education and training programs. This content will be used for newsletters and website updates.

• Keep current participants and alumni informed and connected to new engagement opportunities. The Program Associate will use program listservs for communication.

• Build relationships with North Star Fund’s donor community. The Program Associate will help to grow the community. They will also help sustain the support and engagement of long-term supporters.

Required Skills

• Deep social justice values and a demonstrated commitment to the practice of racial justice, inclusion, and community-driven change

• Fluency with related concepts around intersectionality, structural, institutional, and internalized racism

• Knowledge of and commitment to grassroots organizing led by communities of color

• Resilience, flexibility, humility, self-awareness, and a sense of humor

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills

• Excellent writing, reading comprehension and analytical skills

• Highly organized project manager, able to coordinate multiple moving parts, manage timelines and maintain accurate data systems

• Ability to collaborate across teams to implement cohesive donor programming

• Adaptability and problem solving skills with the ability to adjust plans based on donor needs, team priorities, or shifting movement conditions

• Ability to quickly connect, build trust and develop authentic relationships with people from diverse backgrounds

• Commitment to engage in ongoing political education and skill development

• Proficiency with standard office software (such as Word, Excel or Google Worksuite), video conferencing platforms (Zoom or Meet), and internal communications platforms (Slack, Microsoft Teams)

• Familiarity with presentation software (such as PowerPoint, Canva or Google Slides)

• Familiarity with data management systems such as Airtable or Salesforce

Desired Skills

• Experience managing volunteers

• Community organizing or movement building experience

• Experience with organizing and handling administrative tasks/multitasking, project planning and execution

• Familiarity with grassroots fundraising, individual giving and/or family philanthropy

• Comfort facilitating groups, designing agendas and supporting collective learning

Physical Requirements

Must be able to work at a computer screen for several hours a day. Must be able to attend events, including some travel in the region and beyond, and meet with donors in person and/or via teleconferencing. Occasional evening and weekend events as needed. Light lifting for in-person events may be required. Accommodations will be made as necessary for the safety and well-being of all employees.

Compensation

The salary for this position is $73,337 depending on experience and in accordance with North Star Fund’s compensation structure. North Star Fund offers generous benefits. Benefits include:

• 100% premium paid for medical, dental, and vision insurance

• monthly transportation, cell phone and internet allowance

• flex-time, vacation and holidays

North Star Fund operates within a 32-hour full-time work week.

Additional Information

North Star Fund uses a 32-hour work week for full-time employees. Our work days run Monday through Thursday with periodic evening and weekend work required at times. This position will report to the Donor Organizing Director and will regularly partner with other staff. North Star Fund currently uses a hybrid work model: staff work from home and from our office located in midtown Manhattan. The Program Associate is expected to be available for meetings and events in the communities we serve.

Residency Requirement

All staff are required to periodically attend in-person meetings and events in NYC and the Hudson Valley. Applicants must live in the Hudson Valley or New York City or be within a one-hour commute to these areas.

How to Apply

Please share a resume and a cover letter that shares your interest in the role. More information and application instructions can be found at www.northstarfund.org/jobs. We appreciate all submissions, but please be advised that our capacity allows us to only respond to those best qualified for the position.

Position will remain open until filled but first review of applications will be October 12, 2026.

North Star Fund is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate against applicants based on race, religion, color, disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, gender identity or expression, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), age, veteran status or other legally protected characteristics.

North Star Fund is firmly committed to equity and diversity. We’re committed to the recruitment and retention of people from backgrounds traditionally excluded from philanthropy. We strongly encourage Black, Indigenous and people of color, women, LGBTQ people, elders and differently-abled candidates to apply.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer/Senior Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:

Our portfolio of image sensors can be found in many high-performance imaging applications like space exploration, medical x-ray, sciences, quantum computing, machine vision, low light, and 360 situational awareness.

We are seeking a Manufacturing Engineer/ Senior Manufacturing Engineer to develop, implement, and maintain cost effective manufacturing and test methods, and flow of material for existing products and new product introductions. Utilizes experience in semiconductor assembly and test manufacturing and performs as subject matter expert in relevant manufacturing processes.  This role supports the development of new methods, processes, and equipment and communicates process and production status information and feedback to internal customers and managers.

Primary Responsibilities

• Demonstrated ability to proactively identify opportunities to improve performance, develop targets and action plans and lead an organization to achieve results

• Demonstrated ability to efficiently and effectively monitor operations with excellent communication (verbal and written) and presentation skills

• Experience in electronics/semiconductor environment with hands-on experience CMOS and CCD imagers and cameras a plus

BS and minimum of 7 years' experience as Manufacturing or Process Engineer in electronics manufacturing, including assembly and test.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (Ruby on Rails)
jobs.description:
At PrizePicks, we are the fastest-growing sports company in North America, as recognized by Inc. 5000. As the leading platform for Daily Fantasy Sports, we cover a diverse range of sports leagues, including the NFL, NBA, and Esports titles like League of Legends and Counter-Strike. Our team of over 550 employees thrives in an inclusive culture that values individuals from diverse backgrounds, regardless of their level of sports fandom. Ready to reimagine the DFS industry together?

Senior Software Engineer (Ruby on Rails)

Overview

At PrizePicks, we are changing the game in daily fantasy sports. We are a passionate team of innovators dedicated to creating a best-in-class experience for our members. Our engineering team builds and scales the platform that powers our explosive growth—from our consumer-facing app to the services that support millions of members. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Social Experience team and help us continue to build the future of fantasy sports.

Job Summary

The Social Experience team builds the backend systems behind profiles, feeds, and other social features that help members create an identity, connect with others, and discover and share activity across PrizePicks.

In this role, you will work across mature Rails systems and a growing set of Go and other purpose-built services. You will evolve existing capabilities, define clear service boundaries, and design new backend systems that can scale with our social experiences.

You will own complex work from technical design through production, translate ambiguous product goals into executable plans, influence technical direction, and elevate the engineers around you. This role is for someone who is comfortable extending a mature Rails codebase while helping shape the services that will support the next generation of social experiences at PrizePicks.

What You’ll Do

• Design and build backend services: Architect and implement performant, scalable, and reliable backend systems, primarily in Rails and in Go where appropriate, supporting high-throughput workloads, complex business logic, and evolving social experiences.

• Evolve service boundaries: Help identify and extract well-scoped capabilities from existing Rails systems, designing clear interfaces and incremental migration paths that preserve reliability and backward compatibility.

• Connect product and data systems: Design reliable data flows between backend services and warehouses such as BigQuery and Snowflake, making derived data available without adding latency or reliability risk to member-facing experiences.

• Own technical delivery: Lead complex initiatives from discovery and technical design through implementation, rollout, monitoring, and iteration. Break work into executable pieces, clarify sequencing and ownership, and keep risks and dependencies visible.

• Drive cross-team execution: Partner closely with Product, Design, QA, Data, Platform, and engineers across domains to resolve ambiguity, coordinate dependencies, and move shared work forward.

• Drive system reliability: Diagnose and resolve performance bottlenecks, optimize database queries, and improve the resilience of backend systems under load.

• Define technical direction: Propose and drive architectural decisions for your team’s services, evaluating tradeoffs and communicating recommendations clearly.

• Mentor and elevate: Provide hands-on mentorship to engineers on your team through code reviews, pairing, design discussions, and technical guidance.

• Improve engineering practices: Raise the bar for code quality, testing, observability, deployment, and operational ownership.

• Participate in on-call rotation: Share responsibility for production incidents, contributing to root cause analysis and long-term reliability improvements.

What You Have

Experience:

• 5–8 years of professional software engineering experience, with significant time building production Ruby on Rails applications

• Proven track record of owning and delivering complex, multi-component features in a team environment

• Experience designing and operating backend systems that handle significant scale and complexity

• Experience coordinating technical work across team boundaries and proactively managing dependencies, risks, and changing requirements

Technical Skills:

• Expert-level Ruby on Rails proficiency — you understand the framework deeply, write idiomatic Ruby, and know when to leverage or work around Rails conventions

• Strong proficiency with PostgreSQL, including schema design, query optimization, and performance tuning at scale

• Solid understanding of API design — RESTful services, serialization strategies, and versioning

• Experience with background job processing (Sidekiq or similar) and asynchronous workflows

• Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment automation

• Understanding of observability practices — logging, metrics, tracing

• Working knowledge of Go — our backend includes significant Go services, and cross-stack capability is valued at this level

Working Style:

• You turn ambiguous problems into clear plans, make progress visible, and proactively surface decisions, risks, and dependencies

• You enjoy collaborative problem-solving and are effective at bringing people together, incorporating different perspectives, and building alignment

• You communicate clearly and consistently, translating technical decisions for engineers, partners, and non-technical stakeholders

• You balance deep technical execution with planning, mentorship, reviews, and the broader needs of the team

• You are comfortable operating autonomously in a distributed engineering organization while staying closely connected to teammates and partners

What Makes You Stand Out

• Experience leading the extraction of capabilities from a monolith or evolving systems toward well-defined services

• Experience building social or relationship-driven systems such as feeds, follows, live chat, reactions, activity streams, or recommendations

• Experience designing stat-driven profile systems, including aggregations, rollups, and derived metrics at scale

• Experience building social systems for rapid experimentation through feature flags, ranking experiments, or growth loops

• Experience designing graph-shaped data models and fan-out strategies at scale

• Demonstrated ability to influence technical direction across teams and domains while driving shared initiatives to completion

• Experience leveraging AI-assisted development tools across the development lifecycle — coding, planning, scoping, and code review

• Experience integrating AI tooling into engineering workflows to accelerate team productivity

Where You’ll Live

While we prefer candidates based in Atlanta, we are open to qualified applicants from anywhere in the U.S. and are willing to consider remote candidates. #LI-Remote

Working at PrizePicks

The typical salary range for this position is $175,000 to $185,000. At PrizePicks, we consider your role, level, and where you’ll be working when determining our salary ranges. jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer - Factory Orchestration
jobs.description:
Intrinsic is an AI robotics group at Google aiming to reimagine the potential of industrial robotics. Our team believes that advances in AI, perception and simulation will redefine what’s possible for industrial robotics in the near future – with software and data at the core.

Our mission is to make industrial robotics intelligent, accessible, and usable for millions more businesses, entrepreneurs, and developers. We are a dynamic team of engineers, roboticists, designers, and technologists who are passionate about unlocking the creative and economic potential of industrial robotics.

Role

The Intrinsic Factory Experience is an integrated human interface to define, manage, and monitor highly orchestrated factory operations. We build tools to help forward-thinking factories deploy intelligent, flexible manufacturing workflows at scale. Our tools help manufacturing process designers to optimize their resources, factory managers to make sense of their operations, and floor workers to strategically direct their attention.

We are seeking a highly skilled Full Stack Software Engineer to join our dynamic Factory Orchestration team. In this role, you will be responsible for not only developing human-machine user interfaces (HMI), but also optimizing the performance and functionality of client-side rendering, server-side databases, and integration with other backend APIs in Intrinsic. You will develop the full stack of web interfaces for end-to-end factory orchestration tasks and play a vital role in the development of our frontend libraries and components, ensuring a cohesive and user-friendly experience for all customers. The interfaces you build will shape our product and the role of the human in it.

You are excited by the prospect of owning critical pieces of our user experience (including collaborating with the Product and Design teams, and developing tests). You have excellent development skills across the web application stack and are excited to be part of a world-class, innovative, frontend team.

How your work moves the mission forward

• Develop intuitive and innovative interfaces in collaboration with Product, Design, and Engineering teams.

• Own the full stack of the Intrinsic Factory Experience web application, from database design to user interactions.

• Build and maintain the backend logic and infrastructure of the frontend, including server-side functionality and client-side state management.

• Monitor and improve the health (performance, robustness) of the Intrinsic Factory Experience.

Skills you will need to be successful

• At least 3 years of experience with frontend web engineering, including proficiency in building client-side (TypeScript/Javascript) software.

• Extensive experience in building the full-stack, including server-side (Rust, Go, Python, etc.) software.

• Experience with building visually-rich web applications that enable deep user interactions.

• Familiar with integrating databases, user-access control, and basic authentication/authorization into web apps.

• Ability to work with Rust, both for backends and compiled to web assembly for front ends.

Skills that will differentiate your candidacy

• Experience integrating web apps with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and/or Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).

• Experience building dashboards aimed at various user personas.

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT OBSERVABLE SPACE

At Observable Space, we're redefining how humanity observes and connects with the universe. We're a vertically integrated, high-growth, space technology company building industry-leading precision optics platforms for Earth and in space. Our systems are trusted by thousands of customers, including NASA, JPL, SpaceX, Boeing, RTX, the US Space Force and the U.S. Department of War, leading research institutions and international partners.

We combine precision opto-mechanical hardware, embedded compute, cloud orchestration, and developer-friendly APIs into world class products at scale with in-house manufacturing. From advanced ground stations, on-orbit sensor suites, free space optical lasercom, to distributed compute platforms, we deliver the foundational systems enabling continuous, real-time navigation, observation, and communication in space.

Observable Space is backed by top-tier institutional investors including Lux Capital, Upfront Ventures, RTX Ventures, Detroit Venture Partners and Embedded Ventures. To learn more, visit observable.space http://observable.space.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Electrical Engineer to join our dynamic team. This role will involve deep engagement with our product line of telescopes and observatory hardware. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in circuit fundamentals, with specific expertise in printed circuit board (PCB) design, wire harnessing, circuit simulation, and design for manufacturing (DFM). This role will report to the Director of Electrical Engineering.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and develop electronic circuits, PCBs, and wire harnesses for telescope and observatory hardware.

 - Perform circuit simulations, schematic capture, and layout reviews to ensure functionality, reliability, and manufacturability.

 - Apply best practices for signal integrity, EMI/EMC compliance, and power distribution.

 - Build and test prototypes, including PCB bring-up, rework, and modification (soldering, trace cutting, wiring).

 - Develop and execute test procedures for electrical subsystems, ensuring design meets performance and safety requirements.

 - Perform root cause analysis and debugging using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and spectrum analyzers.

 - Collaborate with mechanical, software, and manufacturing teams to integrate electrical designs into complete systems.

 - Define and document electrical interfaces, block diagrams, product requirements, assembly drawings, and other supporting documents to support cross-team integration.

 - Support design for manufacturing (DFM) and design for reliability (DFR) reviews to ensure smooth transition from prototype to production.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 2+ years of experience in a relevant electrical engineering role.

 - Strong understanding of DC power circuits, motor drivers, common interfaces/protocols (I2C, SPI, CAN, Ethernet, MIPI, PCIe), ADCs, microcontrollers, opamps, and transistor circuits.

 - Excellent circuit debugging skills, knowledge of power supplies, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, spectrum analyzers, multimeters.

 - Comfortable with PCB rework including soldering, staking, cutting traces, preparing wires.

 - Experience with circuit simulation and design tools.

 - Understanding of circuit board construction, transmission line structures, signal integrity, EMI/EMC, via types, and component types.

 - Experience with Altium (or similar PCB software) and LTSpice (or similar software).

 - Understanding of wire harnessing fundamentals such as electrical checkout, hi-pot testing, impedance characterization, and shielding.

 - Acute product sense, placing an emphasis on design for manufacturing and field reliability.

 - Ability to thrive in a fast paced dynamic environment where rapid prototyping is the norm.

 - An iterative mindset- perfect is the enemy of good.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with signal integrity simulation software (Hyperlynx, SIwave).

 - Experience with electromagnetics simulation software (ADS, HFSS).

 - Real world experience with DSPs and ultra high speed conversion and amplification circuitry (100+GHz)

 - Experience with high-reliability validation testing campaigns.

 - Experience with high speed SerDes interface design and testing.

 - Experience mitigating mechanical failure points for PCBs in vibration environments.

 - A love of astronomy, physics, and science.





WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Compensation – A salary package aligned with industry standards and your experience.

Equity Opportunities – Take part in our success with stock options.

Flexible Work Environment – Enjoy working from our office or in a hybrid work setup with the flexibility to work remotely part of the week. We require a minimum of 3 days per week in our office to support collaboration and team culture. (LA Office only)

Unlimited PTO (exempt only) – Take the time you need with our flexible, trust-based vacation policy, including paid holidays. We encourage everyone to rest, recharge, and take care of themselves.

Health & Wellness – Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with 100% of the premium paid by the employer for employees.

Cutting-Edge Tools – Get access to the latest hardware and software you need to do your best work.

Mission-Driven Culture – Be part of a team working on meaningful challenges with real-world impact.

Inclusive Team – We foster a supportive and diverse workplace where all voices are valued.



Observable Space is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Staff Product Analyst (Product-Led Growth)
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.




COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.



Deepgram is looking for a Staff Product Analyst to accelerate our evolution from a single-product transcription company to a comprehensive voice AI platform. You'll be the first product analyst on our team, reporting to our VP of Product and partnering directly with product managers and designers to build the measurement infrastructure and experimentation frameworks that help us scale product-led growth and product adoption.

As the founding analyst, you'll establish the analytics foundation for our product team—building pipelines, defining frameworks, and creating the systems that help product managers, designers, and engineers make faster, and more impactful decisions. You'll start with a laser focus on our PLG funnel, driving conversion from signup to first programmatic API/SDK request, knowing that this optimization directly feeds both PLG revenue and sales-qualified leads. As you establish this foundation, your scope will expand to help identify patterns across our multi-product portfolio and inform strategic investment decisions.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the analytics strategy for product-led growth—design experiments, build measurement infrastructure, and drive insights that increase conversion from signup to first programmatic request

 - Build robust, repeatable analytics pipelines and dashboards from the ground up using Superset and Heap Analytics

 - Partner directly with product managers and designers to define success metrics, establish baselines, and instrument products correctly

 - Design and analyze experiments across the developer journey, with deep understanding of API/SDK adoption patterns

 - Collaborate with analytics partners in Marketing and Sales to connect product usage signals with acquisition, activation, and downstream sales outcomes, building a holistic view of the end-to-end PLG funnel

 - Surface patterns in product usage across our growing portfolio to identify high-value use cases, customer segments, and where to double down on investment

 - Serve as the analytical partner to Product leadership: synthesize insights across multiple products and use cases to identify patterns that inform longer-term product strategy and investment decisions

 - Establish experimentation best practices and analytical rigor as the team scales PLG motions

 - Translate complex findings into clear, actionable recommendations that shape product roadmap and investment decisions

 - Build the analytics muscle for the team—creating frameworks and systems that enable PMs to PLG insights while you focus on strategic analysis




YOU'LL LOVE THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have the seniority and leadership to define what "good" looks like for product analytics at Deepgram

 - Get energized by being the first—building systems from scratch and establishing foundational practices

 - Can balance deep analytical work with strategic pattern recognition across a multi-product portfolio

 - Have strong opinions on experimentation methodology and PLG measurement, backed by experience

 - Thrive in ambiguity and can define the right questions to ask, not just answer requests

 - Love partnering closely with product leadership to shape strategy in real-time

 - Bring natural customer empathy and curiosity, as well as openness to try new tools/AI workflows to maximize analytics efficiency
   
   


IT'S IMPORTANT TO US THAT YOU HAVE

 - Staff-level expertise in product analytics, with proven ability to lead analytics strategy (we care more about expertise and leadership than years of experience)

 - Demonstrated track record of accelerating PLG growth at a previous company, particularly driving conversion in developer-focused products

 - Strong SQL skills and hands-on experience working directly with data warehouses

 - Proven ability to build dashboards and analytics infrastructure yourself—you don't need a data engineering team to be effective

 - Deep experience designing, running, and analyzing experiments with statistical rigor

 - Understanding of developer behavior and API/SDK adoption patterns—you know what signals matter for programmatic usage

 - Experience being the first or founding analyst on a team—comfortable building everything from scratch

 - Leadership presence to establish best practices and mentor PMs on data literacy

 - Excellent communication skills to translate technical findings into strategic recommendations for executives
   
   


IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAD

 - Experience with Superset and Heap Analytics (or similar tools like Mixpanel, Amplitude, Looker, Mode)

 - Background in B2B SaaS with both PLG and enterprise motions

 - Understanding of multi-product portfolio dynamics and how to measure cross-product patterns

 - Experience with usage-based pricing models or real-time streaming data products

 - Deep knowledge of product instrumentation and event tracking best practices

 - Expertise in advanced statistical methods beyond basic A/B testing (causal inference, cohort analysis, time-series analysis)

 - Experience working in voice AI, ML/AI platforms, or developer tools

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com http://deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

jobs.title: Recycling Centre Attendant- Christmas Casual Perth
jobs.description:
Join our team as a Christmas Casual across our Perth depots!

Love staying active, meeting new people, and working in a fast-paced environment? We’d love to hear from you. At TOMRA, every day is different, and we’re looking for friendly, reliable team members who are ready to get involved and make a difference.

As a Christmas Casual, you'll play an important role in keeping our depot running smoothly during our busiest time of year. You'll welcome customers, assist them with recycling their containers, help them use our reverse vending machines, and create a positive experience every time they visit.
