jobs.title: Sr. Total Rewards Manager
jobs.description:
Hi! I’m Rachel and I lead People Operations here at Ashby. I recently joined and I’m excited that we're expanding our team! The People Operations Team provides support to Ashby employees through the development and implementation of programs, policies, and services that contribute to a productive and inclusive working environment. We ensure that the work we do aligns with our Operating Principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles#operating-principles and strengthens the environment we're building at Ashby. Our approach is to do things differently – we prioritize what truly fits our team and enhances how we work together. By embracing creativity and customization, we aim to create a people-first culture that drives both individual and organizational success.

We review all applications, and there isn’t a benefit to applying quickly. Take your time, look at the application questions and please submit before the application deadline! We aren’t able to take calls outside of the interview process, so reaching out to the team won’t push your application forward.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced Total Rewards leader to build and own Ashby’s total rewards function through our next phase of growth.

This is a builder’s role. Some of the foundation is in place; a lot of it isn’t. You’ll set the philosophy, design the frameworks, build the infrastructure, and run the work day to day. It’s a chance to shape how a company rewards its people rather than administer decisions someone else made.

It’s also unusually analytical, and unusually creative. Ashby’s Total Rewards philosophy is principled and intentionally not one-size-fits-all: approaches vary by function, because different parts of the business compete in different talent markets. Total Rewards partners closely with leadership to provide the structure, documentation, guidance, and governance that keep those approaches equitable, competitive, and scalable. The upshot is that the most interesting problems here don’t have off-the-shelf answers. How do you price a role that survey data doesn’t cover? How do you keep a flexible system fair and explainable? How do you tell, early, that one talent market has moved while the others haven’t? You’ll need real fluency with data, the discipline to structure a problem before you solve it, and the confidence to invent the model when no model exists.

A lot of this work looks less like administering a program and more like a well-run strategy engagement: frame the question, get the data, build the model, pressure-test the answer, and bring leaders a recommendation with the tradeoffs made explicit. The difference is that here you also go implement it.

You’ll partner closely with People Ops, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Legal, and functional leaders to design programs that support how Ashby attracts, retains, and rewards exceptional people — building a more scalable approach while preserving the flexibility each part of the business needs.

We’re looking for someone who has built and scaled Total Rewards in high-growth, VC-backed SaaS companies and is energized by all three of philosophy, systems, and execution — someone who would rather go build the analysis than wait for it.

This role starts as an individual contributor and is expected to grow into people management as the function scales.




YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

Building Ashby’s compensation infrastructure

Bands, leveling alignment, market positioning, review cadences, benchmarking methodology, and clear guidance for offers, promotions, refreshers, and market adjustments — globally, and in partnership with founders, executives, and functional leaders. Some areas are mature; others are still forming. You’ll bring structure to the ambiguity with frameworks that are principled, practical, and hold up under scrutiny. You will be responsible for helping leaders reason through tradeoffs, bringing them a clear recommendation and the logic behind it, and documenting the non-standard rather than handing anyone a rule book.

Reading the market and helping Ashby adapt quickly

Combine market data, internal data, and outside signals to allow us to respond quickly and at scale when conditions change. Build the mechanisms that catch market movement across the whole company, not just the functions with the loudest signals: find the gaps in survey coverage, spot which teams are repricing faster than others, form a view on why, and turn what you see into a recommendation.

Owning Total Rewards strategy end-to-end

Compensation, equity, benefits, and perks. With founders and company leaders, define the philosophy, principles, and long-term direction for how we reward people globally. Evaluate our programs continuously and make recommendations that balance market competitiveness, internal equity, business needs, and long-term sustainability — framed the way a good strategy memo is framed: the options, the tradeoffs, and where you land.

Leading benefits strategy and administration

Own global benefits end to end: strategy, selection, renewals, plan design, competitiveness assessment, broker and vendor management, and the systems and processes behind a strong employee experience.

Leading equity program infrastructure

Partner with Finance and company leadership to bring structure, consistency, and scalability to equity practices, support program administration, and help employees understand how equity fits within the broader Total Rewards picture.

Building scalable systems and operations

Improve the systems, workflows, documentation, and operational processes behind Total Rewards. You will work in tools like CandorIQ, Pave, and OpenComp. You will use automation, AI, and good operational design to get roles to market quickly, support pay decisions efficiently, and keep the underlying data trustworthy.

Acting as a trusted cross-functional partner

You’re the subject matter expert for Total Rewards at Ashby. You’ll help leaders navigate rewards decisions with sound judgment, fairness, and clarity — and make complicated questions land simply in front of founders and executives.

Preparing the function to scale

You begin as a hands-on functional owner, but you’ll build with future scale in mind by establishing the documentation, operating rhythms, standards, and decision-making frameworks the function will need as it grows, and flagging the organizational needs ahead.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You bring several years of progressive Total Rewards experience, including meaningful ownership of compensation, benefits, and equity programs in high-growth organizations and you’ve built compensation infrastructure from the ground up.

 - You bring an analytical first mindset. You build the model, pressure-test your own numbers, and would rather run the analysis yourself than wait for someone else to.

 - You’re a structured thinker. You take a messy question, break it into the parts that matter, form a hypothesis, and test it — and you can walk someone through your reasoning without losing them.

 - You’re a creative problem solver in the comp space. When benchmarks are thin or the role is new, you reason from first principles and design the approach that fits the problem and not the one you used last time.

 - You’re comfortable where some principles are centralized and other elements are tailored by function, and you can keep that flexibility equitable and explainable.

 - You’ve built and scaled compensation frameworks and benefits programs for globally distributed organizations, ideally through periods of significant growth.

 - You can support leaders with different needs and viewpoints while holding the line on trust, consistency, and decision quality.

 - You’re highly effective at both strategy and execution, and comfortable being the primary owner of the work day to day.

 - You’re an exceptional communicator who can make complex Total Rewards topics land with any audience and can show the reasoning behind a number, not just the number. You’re comfortable putting a recommendation in front of founders and defending it.

 - You’re detail-oriented and operationally strong, always looking for ways to improve systems, processes, and program quality.

 - You’ve led or managed others, or you’re excited to build and eventually scale a Total Rewards team.


BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience building and scaling global compensation and benefits programs across multiple regions and employment models.

 - Experience using automation, AI, and technology to make Total Rewards operations faster, more accurate, and more scalable.

 - Strong modeling and data skills beyond the standard toolkit including advanced spreadsheet work, SQL, Python, or BI tools.

 - A background that blends Total Rewards with strategy consulting, corporate finance or FP&A, or people analytics. We value people who have been trained to structure and solve ambiguous problems, wherever they learned to do it.

 - Experience with tools such as CandorIQ, Pave, and OpenComp.


THIS ROLE MAY NOT BE A FIT IF

 - You want to bring your own Total Rewards playbook and install it at Ashby, rather than reimagine and evolve what’s already been started.

 - You prefer operating inside highly standardized programs to building and adapting them in a more flexible environment.

 - You’re less interested in the hands-on work of running the function — including doing the analysis yourself.

 - You reach for the benchmark before the reasoning, or you need rigid rules to make a call.

 - You’d rather present the data than the recommendation.

 - You’re uncomfortable making decisions in ambiguity or helping leaders through nuanced compensation questions.

 - Your experience is concentrated in one area of Total Rewards, with limited exposure across compensation, equity, and benefits.

 - You’re not energized by partnering across functions, balancing competing perspectives, and shaping practical solutions.

 - Most of your experience is in mature organizations with established programs, processes, and teams, without having had to build infrastructure through growth and change.


INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is thorough — we aim to ensure each person joining the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows:

 - Recruiter Screen with Talent Acquisition Team - 30 minutes

 - Hiring Manager Interview - 45 minutes

 - Take Home Assignment
   
   - Followed by 1 hour live session to discuss

 - Virtual Onsite - 2.5-3 hours

 - Final Round with CEO - 30 minutes


ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of recruiting software and we’re starting with a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run an efficient and data-driven hiring process. We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom.  We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀




BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅.

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Revenue Cycle Specialist
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Revenue Cycle Specialist is responsible for supporting the organization's revenue cycle operations through billing, collections, payment reconciliation, and related financial activities. This role initially focuses on clinical research sponsor billing and collections while partnering closely with Clinical Operations, Finance, and Accounting to ensure accurate billing, timely collections, revenue recognition, and financial reporting.

This position is ideal for someone who enjoys improving financial workflows, leveraging technology to increase efficiency, and supporting accurate and scalable revenue cycle processes within a growing healthcare organization. The successful candidate will have a strong analytical mindset, attention to detail, and the ability to identify opportunities to improve workflows, reduce manual processes, and enhance operational effectiveness.

As the organization grows, this role may support additional revenue cycle functions, including claims processing, payment posting, reimbursement support, and other financial operations.

Key Responsibilities

Revenue Cycle & Financial Operations

 - Prepare, submit, and manage sponsor invoices based on executed clinical trial agreements, study budgets, payment milestones, and contractual terms.

 - Monitor accounts receivable and proactively follow up with sponsors regarding outstanding balances to ensure timely collections.

 - Manage high-volume email communication and maintain professional, timely follow-up with sponsors and internal stakeholders.

 - Reconcile sponsor payments to bank deposits and investigate payment discrepancies.

 - Assist with revenue journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting documentation as part of the month-end close process.

 - Maintain accurate billing, payment, and financial records within CRIO and other applicable systems.

Clinical Research Finance Support

 - Perform quality control (QC) reviews of clinical research budgets within CRIO to ensure alignment with executed contracts, sponsor agreements, payment schedules, and billing requirements.

 - Review contracts, budgets, amendments, and payment terms to validate billing triggers and revenue expectations.

 - Partner with Clinical Operations to resolve billing questions and ensure accurate financial tracking of research activities.

Process Improvement & Automation

 - Evaluate existing revenue cycle workflows and leverage technology, automation tools, and data analysis to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, scalability, and reporting.

 - Develop and implement process improvements that reduce manual effort and streamline billing, reconciliation, and reporting activities.

 - Identify trends, recurring issues, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Additional Revenue Cycle Support

 - Support additional revenue cycle activities as business needs evolve, including claims processing, specialty pharmacy payment posting, reimbursement activities, and other financial operations.

 - Assist with refinement and optimization of revenue cycle processes across additional business lines.

Qualifications

 - 3–5 years of experience in Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), healthcare finance, clinical research finance, accounts receivable, medical billing, or a related field.

 - Experience managing billing, collections, payment reconciliation, and accounts receivable processes.

 - Advanced Microsoft Excel skills required, including proficiency with complex formulas, PivotTables, data analysis, reconciliations, and reporting.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.

 - Demonstrated ability to identify process improvement opportunities and implement more efficient workflows.

 - Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and high-volume communication independently.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

 - Ability to work collaboratively across teams.

Preferred

 - Experience with clinical research sponsor billing or clinical trial financial management.

 - Experience reviewing contracts, budgets, amendments, and payment schedules.

 - Experience performing quality control (QC) reviews of clinical research budgets.

 - Experience with CRIO or another Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS).

 - Accounting experience, including journal entries, account reconciliations, and month-end close support.

 - Experience with workflow automation, reporting tools, or process optimization initiatives.

 - Experience with healthcare claims processing, payer workflows, denials management, reimbursement processes, or other healthcare revenue cycle functions.

jobs.description:
At EdSights, we're building the technology for higher education to understand what students are actually thinking and feeling, so they can act before small struggles become big problems. We call it Student Voice Intelligence: engaging students in real-time, AI-powered conversations, uncovering the real drivers of attrition, and delivering those insights to power student success and enrollment workflows.



Today, we partner with 300+ colleges and universities across the country. We're backed by an $80M investment https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250925255277/en/EdSights-Raises-%2480M-to-Lead-the-Next-Era-of-Student-Engagement-and-Retention-Software-in-Higher-Education from JMI Equity and are in a phase of rapid execution and expansion. This is an opportunity to do meaningful, hands-on work at a high-growth startup https://www.inc.com/profile/edsights tackling one of higher education's most urgent challenges: helping more students persist from enrollment through graduation.



You’ll join a driven, thoughtful team that values ownership, moves quickly, and cares deeply about building products that make a measurable difference for students.



“EdSights has perhaps the world’s most valuable data set on what college students need to navigate their academic lives.”

          - The Washington Post

jobs.title: Payroll & Benefits Specialist
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Payroll & Benefits Specialist is responsible for the organization's payroll and benefits operations, including timely and accurate payroll processing, state and local payroll tax compliance, benefits administration, open enrollment, reconciliations, reporting, and employee support. The Payroll & Benefits Specialist will work closely with Finance & Accounting, employees, benefits providers, and Rippling or comparable system to resolve issues, maintain compliance, and ensure efficient and effective operations.

The ideal candidate is highly detail-oriented, comfortable working independently, and able to exercise sound judgment in managing sensitive, time-critical financial and employee matters. They enjoy improving processes, leveraging technology, and building efficient and scalable payroll and benefits operations.

Key Responsibilities

Payroll Processing & Operations

 - Manage the end-to-end payroll process, including regular, off-cycle, bonus, and other payrolls as needed.

 - Review and validate payroll inputs, including new hires, terminations, compensation changes, deductions, benefits, PTO, reimbursements, garnishments, and other payroll adjustments.

 - Perform thorough reviews to ensure payroll is accurate, complete, and processed on schedule.

 - Investigate and resolve payroll discrepancies and employee payroll questions in a timely and professional manner.

 - Partner with Finance & Accounting on payroll reporting, reconciliations, journal entries, and month-end close activities.

 - Participate in reviews of acquisition targets on an as needed basis to help highlight areas where potential selling organizations are deficient in payroll compliance.

Payroll Tax Compliance

 - Monitor state and local filing requirements, deadlines, tax rates, and regulatory changes.

 - Complete state tax registrations for new-state expansions, coordinating timely registration with state agencies and ensuring ongoing payroll tax filings are handled accurately and compliantly.

 - Coordinate with third-party tax filer on state and local payroll tax notices, agency correspondence, and compliance issues.

 - Proactively manage new filing requirements as the Company grows and enters new jurisdictions.

Benefits Administration & Open Enrollment

 - Manage the day-to-day administration of the organization's employee benefit programs, including medical, dental, vision, life, disability, retirement, and other benefits as applicable.

 - Serve as the primary point of contact for employees regarding benefits eligibility, enrollment, qualifying life events, deductions, and general benefits questions.

 - Partner with benefits brokers, carriers, third-party administrators, and other external providers to resolve enrollment, eligibility, billing, and employee issues.

 - Support annual open enrollment with Accounting leadership, including system setup, employee communications, and reconciliation.

 - Process benefit enrollments, changes, and terminations in Rippling and with applicable benefit providers.

 - Reconcile benefit deductions, employer contributions, and carrier invoices.

 - Maintain accurate benefits records and ensure timely updates for new hires, terminations, leaves, and other employee status changes.

Process Improvement & Automation

 - Develop and implement process improvements that reduce manual effort and streamline payroll, tax compliance, benefits administration, reconciliations, and reporting activities.

 - Identify trends, recurring issues, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

 - Help optimize the use of Rippling and other systems to improve payroll and benefits workflows, controls, reporting, and employee experience.

Qualifications

 - 3-5 years of payroll, payroll tax, benefits administration, accounting, or related experience.

 - Proven ability to independently manage payroll for a multi-state employee population.

 - Strong knowledge of state and local payroll tax compliance, including filings, payments, registrations, reconciliations, and tax notices.

 - Knowledge of employee benefits administration, including enrollments, qualifying life events, deductions, and provider coordination.

 - Ability to manage or support annual open enrollment.

 - Proficiency with a payroll or HRIS platform; Rippling experience strongly preferred.

 - Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.

 - Ability to independently manage multiple priorities, recurring deadlines, and confidential information.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

 - Ability to work collaboratively with Finance & Accounting, employees, and external payroll and benefits providers.

Preferred

 - Rippling Payroll and Benefits experience.

 - Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including complex formulas, PivotTables, data analysis, reconciliations, and reporting.

 - Familiarity with multiple state and local payroll tax jurisdictions.

 - Experience handling payroll tax notices, audits, registrations, and agency correspondence.

 - Accounting experience, including journal entries, account reconciliations, and month-end close support.

 - Experience with payroll and benefits reporting and reconciliation.

 - Experience with workflow automation, reporting tools, or process optimization initiatives.

Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Test Technician, reporting to the Manager, Hardware Development  to support the development of the systems that will be required for the design and build of artificial-gravity human-rated space stations.

The Hardware Development team takes pride in crafting cutting-edge mechanisms, fluid systems, and electronics to test hardware critical to the Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) to support life onboard our artificial-gravity commercial space station . Client Success Specialist

Commerce, CA | Full-Time | Onsite

Salary range: 75k – 85k

At Ernest, we’ve been helping businesses succeed for more than 80 years by building lasting relationships with our clients, employees, and communities. As the largest privately owned packaging company in the United States, we’ve built our success by putting people first. We believe in promoting from within, investing in our employees, and creating opportunities for people to build meaningful, long-term careers.

We’re looking for a Client Success Specialist to join our Commerce, CA team. If you’re organized, make good decisions, enjoy building relationships, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and take pride in owning your work, we’d love to meet you.

Position Summary

As a Client Success Specialist, you’ll be a key business partner to an assigned portfolio of clients and their primary day-to-day point of contact. Working closely with a Client Relationship Manager (outside sales representative), you’ll take ownership of the ongoing needs of your accounts and help ensure their business runs smoothly.

This role goes well beyond processing orders or handling transactions. You’ll get to know your clients’ businesses, anticipate their needs, solve problems, and make thoughtful decisions about how best to support them. You’ll have the flexibility to manage priorities, recommend solutions, and keep things moving without needing direction at every step.

Ultimately, you’ll own the day-to-day success of your accounts by building strong client relationships, identifying opportunities, resolving issues, and partnering with the Client Relationship Manager to grow the business.

The Client Success Specialist is a full-time, exempt (salaried) position reporting to the Client Coordinator Manager.

What You'll Do

jobs.title: Credit Risk Manager
jobs.description:
About Figure

Figure (NASDAQ: FIGR) is transforming capital markets through blockchain. We’re proving that blockchain isn’t just theory - it’s powering real products used by hundreds of thousands of consumers and institutions.

By combining blockchain’s transparency and efficiency with AI-driven automation, we’ve reimagined how loans are originated, funded, and traded in secondary markets. From faster processing times to lower costs and reduced bias, our technology is helping borrowers, investors, and financial institutions achieve better outcomes.

Together with our 170+ partners, we’ve originated over $22 billion in home equity loans (HELOCs) on our blockchain-native platform, making Figure the largest non-bank provider of home equity financing in the U.S. Figure’s ecosystem also includes YLDS, an SEC-registered yield-bearing stablecoin that operates as a tokenized money market fund, and several other products and platforms that are reshaping consumer finance and capital markets.

We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Most Innovative Fintech Startups in 2025 and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies in Finance and Personal Finance.

About the Role

Join our team as a Credit Risk Manager! In this collaborative, high-visibility role, you will harness cutting-edge analytics and alternative data to transform customer insights into winning strategies for our HELOC and secured lending portfolios. Partnering closely with Capital Markets, Product, Engineering, Servicing, and Compliance, you will oversee credit policies, guide execution, and pioneer creative risk frameworks that safeguard portfolio health while unlocking growth. If you are a proactive problem solver who loves digging deep into lending analytics, exploring novel data sources, and uniting cross-functional teams around portfolio performance, we want to hear from you.

What You’ll Do

• Continuously refine and modernize credit underwriting strategies using advanced analytics to optimize risk decisions across lending products.

• Analyze historical loan performance data to model credit expansion initiatives, identify new customer segments, and optimize funnel conversion.

• Perform root-cause analyses on credit losses and default trends, partnering with Fraud Risk Management to sharpen fraud controls.

• Develop valuation models to estimate segment-level economics and advise Capital Markets on yield projections and performance assumptions.

• Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to design A/B tests that balance risk control, conversion lift, and user experience.

• Track and validate pre- and post-implementation performance for all deployed credit and fraud rule changes.

• Design monitoring frameworks to track new product launches at a granular segment level, identify emerging portfolio risks, and inform executive decision-making.

• Present Figure’s underwriting methodology to investors and serve as a core contact for due diligence and portfolio performance inquiries.

• Collaborate with Legal and Compliance to ensure all credit strategies strictly meet regulatory requirements.

• Conduct ad hoc quantitative analyses to support broader Credit, Operations, and Product objectives.

What We Look For

• Bachelor/Master’s degree with a quantitative background (e.g., Statistics, Math, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, or Business).

• 5+ years in credit risk management or data science within consumer lending.

• Comfortable working in a fast-moving, evolving environment where priorities shift, and initiatives move quickly.

• Self-driven, with intense focus on results. High curiosity with a proven track record of probing root causes, challenging the status quo, and designing out-of-the-box solutions.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, combined with solid business judgment

• Clear, strong communicator who can translate complex data into simple, actionable insights for any audience.

• Strong team player and comfortable interacting with partners across multiple teams and at varying levels of seniority

• Advanced proficiency in SQL and Python/R for pulling, cleaning, and modeling complex relational data independently.

• Practical application of predictive modeling, customer segmentation, and statistical procedures to evaluate risk and borrower behavior.

• Experience with Tableau, Power BI, and Looker.

• Adhere to all company security policies and data handling procedures.

• Complete mandatory security awareness training within required timeframes.

• Promptly report any suspected security incidents or suspicious activity to the Security team.

Salary

• Base Compensation Range: $134,640 - $168,300/yr

• 25% annual bonus target, paid quarterly

• Company equity in the form of RSUs

This is the compensation range for the role in the United States. Actual compensation may vary based on a candidate’s experience, skills, location, internal equity, and evolving business needs. While most offers are generally made within the middle of the range, final compensation is determined based on the factors above.

Benefits

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% employer-paid premiums for employees and their dependents on select plans

• Company HSA, FSA, Dependent Care FSA, 401(k), and commuter benefits

• Employer-paid life and disability insurance

• 11 observed holidays and PTO plan

• Up to 12 weeks of paid family leave

• Continuing education reimbursement

California Residents, please review our California Employee and General Workforce Privacy Notice for further information. By submitting your application, you are agreeing and acknowledging that you have read and understand the above notice.

Figure will not sponsor work visas for this position. In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

jobs.title: Strategic Business Operations Lead, API
jobs.description:
Perplexity's API Platform brings our work in AI, search, and agent orchestration to developers. Our customers range from AI-native startups to some of the world's largest technology companies. Working with them, alongside our own developments in building Perplexity’s core application gives our team direct exposure to how search, models, and tools are used to build and scale AI-native products and applications.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

We are looking for a Strategic Business Operations Lead to manage customer relationships and lead projects that help grow the API business. The role is roughly half customer-facing and half strategic and operational work, with an initial focus on building and improving our post-sale programs.



You will own a portfolio of API customers, learning how AI-native companies and large enterprises evaluate, adopt, and scale AI infrastructure. Working closely with API leadership, you will help shape how the business operates and lead projects such as product migrations, customer enablement, and account coverage. You will put recommendations into practice, with results measured in customer adoption, retention, and growth.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Manage a portfolio of API customer relationships, leading account conversations, understanding business priorities, and coordinating next steps across technical and commercial teams.

 - Build account plans around adoption, value, and growth. Identify risks early and partner with Sales and account owners on renewals and expansion.

 - Design and improve the post-sale operating model, including customer segmentation, account coverage, onboarding, health signals, and handoffs between teams.

 - Lead strategic projects across the API business, with an initial emphasis on customer adoption and retention. Scope the problem, develop a recommendation, coordinate execution, and track outcomes.

 - Run customer programs such as product and endpoint migrations, enablement, and rollout communications. Establish the audience, milestones, internal responsibilities, and follow-up needed for each.

 - Coordinate customer communications for product updates, pricing changes, deprecations, and incidents, working with Engineering, Support, and commercial teams on accurate messaging.

 - Analyze usage, consumption against commitments, renewal risk, and expansion signals to prioritize customer engagement and inform business decisions.

 - Build practical reporting, workflows, and automation that help the team manage a growing customer base. Partner with Finance and Billing Operations to improve the customer experience around credits, commitments, and billing.

 - Bring insights from customers into API planning and take on additional strategic initiatives as business priorities evolve.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of experience in business operations, strategy and operations, consulting, customer success, account management, or a related role.

 - A track record of taking ambiguous business problems from analysis through implementation, including projects that require coordination across multiple teams.

 - Strong analytical skills: comfortable working with spreadsheets, usage data, and business metrics to identify a problem, test a hypothesis, and recommend an action.

 - Strong relationship skills and a genuine interest in spending a substantial part of your time with customers. You can lead a conversation, understand their priorities, and take responsibility for the follow-up.

 - Curiosity about APIs and AI products, with the ability to learn technical concepts and work effectively with engineering teams.

 - Clear writing, commercial judgment, and the ability to balance ongoing customer relationships with longer-term projects.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Direct customer-facing experience in a B2B technology company, including account management, customer success, partnerships, or solutions work.

 - Experience with API businesses, developer platforms, or consumption-based revenue models.

 - Working knowledge of SQL, CRM systems, or BI tools, and experience automating recurring analysis or workflows.

jobs.title: Associate Product Manager
jobs.description:
Associate Product Manager, Workplace Solutions

Santa Clara, CA - Onsite

THE OPPORTUNITY

Picarro is looking for a talented and driven Associate Product Manager to join our Industrial Solutions team at our Santa Clara headquarters. This is an exciting opportunity for an early-to-mid career professional with a strong technical foundation to take meaningful ownership of critical elements of Picarro’s workplace monitoring solution, first supporting parallel go-to-market efforts and subsequent sustaining product management responsibilities.

You will work at the intersection of hardware and software, partnering closely with R&D, engineering, data analytics, sales, field operations, and customer program management teams to define and deliver products that reinforce Picarro's position as the industry leader in data-driven workplace and personal exposure monitoring solutions, reporting to the Director of Application Development/Workplace Product Manager.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Own your product roadmap. Define, prioritize, and communicate a product roadmap for workplace products that balances near-term customer needs with long-term strategic bets, across both hardware and software dimensions.

• Drive market and customer insight. Conduct customer interviews, analyze field and usage data, and synthesize market research to identify high-impact opportunities, validate product concepts, and maintain a deep understanding of the natural gas and energy landscape.

• Write clear requirements. Author Marketing Requirements Documents (MRDs), Product Requirements Documents (PRDs), user stories, and acceptance criteria for both hardware features and software releases.

• Lead cross-functional execution. Partner with R&D, engineering, manufacturing, QA, software development, and data analytics teams to bring products to market on time and within budget.

• Champion Agile delivery. Serve as an active product owner in Agile scrum cycles — participate in sprint planning, backlog grooming, story review, and retrospectives for software and data platform initiatives.

• Support hardware NPI. Collaborate with engineering and operations on New Product Introduction (NPI) and Product Lifecycle (PLC) processes, ensuring smooth transitions from development to production.

• Enable the commercial team. Develop sales collateral, training materials, and competitive positioning to support the gas business team; respond to technical customer inquiries and assist in pre-sales activities.

• Represent Picarro externally. Present products and solutions at industry conferences, trade shows, and customer sites; build lasting relationships with key gas utility accounts and industry stakeholders to collaborate on new product breakthroughs and establish reference standards for the industry.

• Measure success. Define KPIs for product initiatives; track adoption and field performance post-launch and drive continuous improvement based on data and customer feedback.

• Stay ahead of the market. Monitor the competitive landscape, emerging technologies, and regulatory trends in workplace exposure.

REQUIREMENTS

• Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, or a related technical field. M.S. or Ph.D. a plus.

• 2-3 years of experience in product management and overall 3-5 years of experience in applications engineering, or an equivalent role with product ownership responsibilities.

• Hands-on experience managing software, hardware, or ideally both products

• Demonstrated familiarity with Agile software development methodologies

• Experience as a product owner or active participant in sprint-based development.

• Experience with hardware product development processes, including NPI, design verification, and product lifecycle management.

• Ability to comprehend and communicate complex technical concepts clearly to diverse audiences — from engineers and data scientists to executive leadership and non-technical utility customers.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; experience writing MRDs, PRDs, or functional specifications.

• Strong aptitude to articulate and execute on business strategy with a results-oriented, 'make it happen' attitude.

• Willingness to travel domestically and internationally approximately 20% of the time for customer visits, conferences, and trade shows.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• Exposure to regulatory frameworks governing Ethylene Oxide or other acute or chronic hazardous gases, EPA reporting.

• Experience with data analytics products, cloud-based SaaS platforms, or enterprise software for the energy sector.

• Proficiency with product and project management tools such as Jira, Confluence, Pendo, or Figma.

• Prior experience in a startup or high-growth technology company.

The base salary range for this full-time position is $110K to $125K. Our total compensation packages include base salary, bonus eligibility, and equity. Your base salary range and title will be determined based on the location, experience, qualification, skills, knowledge, level, and pay of employees in similar positions.

We offer a comprehensive benefit package including:

• Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance

• Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA) plans

• Life, Short-Term Disability, and Long-Term Disability Insurance

• Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays

• Employee Referral Program

• 401K

• Social events (summer picnic, holiday party, team lunches, etc.)

• On-site Health & Wellness programs (fitness challenges, outdoor bootcamp, flu-shots, etc.)

About Picarro:

We are the world's leader in timely, trusted, and actionable data using enhanced optical spectroscopy. Our solutions are used in a wide variety of applications, including natural gas leak detection, ethylene oxide emissions monitoring, semiconductor fabrication, pharmaceutical, petrochemical, atmospheric science, air quality, greenhouse gas measurements, food safety, hydrology, ecology, and more. Our software and hardware are designed and manufactured in Santa Clara, California and are used in over 90 countries worldwide based on over 65 patents related to cavity ring-down spectroscopy (CRDS) technology and are unparalleled in their precision, ease of use, and reliability.

At Picarro, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. jobs.title: Head of Talent Acquisition
jobs.description:
Apollo.io is the leading go-to-market solution for revenue teams, trusted by over 500,000 companies and millions of users globally, from rapidly growing startups to some of the world's largest enterprises. Founded in 2015, the company is one of the fastest growing companies in SaaS, raising approximately $250 million to date and valued at $1.6 billion. Apollo.io provides sales and marketing teams with easy access to verified contact data for over 210 million B2B contacts and 35 million companies worldwide, along with tools to engage and convert these contacts in one unified platform. By helping revenue professionals find the most accurate contact information and automating the outreach process, Apollo.io turns prospects into customers. Apollo raised a series D in 2023 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and more, and counts the former President and COO of Hubspot, JD Sherman, among its board members.

The Role

We are seeking an experienced Head of Talent Acquisition to join our rapidly growing technology startup. This critical leadership role will be responsible for building and scaling a high-performing global recruiting organization, implementing AI-powered recruiting strategies, and serving as a trusted partner to our executive team. The ideal candidate will combine a deep understanding of talent acquisition best practices with a passion for innovation and automation. • Collaborate with Marketing and People teams to enhance Apollo’s employer brand and attract top-tier candidates.

• Deep familiarity with AI-powered recruiting tools and a track record of using technology to improve recruiting outcomes.

• Strong operational mindset, with expertise in recruiting metrics, process design, and systems implementation.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust and influence at all levels of the organization.

jobs.title: Lead Data Analyst
jobs.description:

This roles partners directly with clients to design, implement, and evolve marketing & data analytics programs. It leads engagements that require integration of multi-channel data, development of insights frameworks, and translates analytics into business outcomes across verticals.

jobs.title: Senior Test Engineer - HIL
jobs.description:
ON.energy is building the backbone of energy and AI infrastructure powering grid-safe data centers and mission-critical facilities. The company supplies and operates hyperscale power systems that solve the toughest resilience challenges, delivering custom solutions for AI data centers, mission-critical facilities, and front-of-the-meter assets. ON recently announced a 5GW partnership, with 3GW currently under construction across multiple hyperscale data center campuses. With patented technology and proprietary software, ON.energy develops projects worldwide that set new benchmarks for resilience.

Role Summary

The HIL Test Engineer develops and operates hardware-in-the-loop and real-time simulation capability for ON.energy storage and power conversion products. The role covers real-time model development, integration of controllers and firmware with the simulation environment, execution of structured test campaigns, and the reporting that supports design reviews and product release. This is a hands-on laboratory and integration role, working closely with the controls, firmware, modeling, and product engineering teams.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain real-time models of plant, grid, and equipment behavior for use in controller testing.

• Configure and operate the HIL environment, including real-time simulator, I/O interfaces, signal conditioning, and data acquisition.

• Integrate product controllers, control software, and firmware builds with the simulation environment, and maintain those configurations under version control.

• Integrate supplier-provided equipment models and develop equivalent models where required.

• Plan and execute functional, performance, fault, boundary-condition, and regression test campaigns against defined acceptance criteria.

• Verify control performance across normal operation, disturbances, abnormal conditions, and recovery.

• Compare test results against offline simulation studies and laboratory measurements, and resolve discrepancies.

• Develop scripts and tooling to automate test execution, data processing, and reporting.

• Investigate failures with controls and firmware engineers, support root-cause analysis, and re-test to closure.

• Prepare test reports documenting method, configuration, results, limitations, and recommendations.

• Maintain laboratory safety, equipment, configuration records, and documentation.

Key Requirements

• Four or more years in HIL testing, real-time simulation, controls validation, or laboratory testing of grid-connected power electronics.

• Bachelor's degree or higher in electrical engineering, power systems, controls engineering, or a related discipline.

• Direct experience on at least one real-time simulation platform, such as RTDS/RSCAD, Typhoon HIL, or OPAL-RT.

• Working capability with offline simulation tools such as MATLAB/Simulink and PSCAD, and an understanding of what has to change when a model is made to run in real time.

• Grounding in inverter controls, energy storage systems, and power system dynamics.

• Python, or a comparable language, used in earnest for test automation and data analysis.

• Test plans, procedures, and acceptance criteria you have authored yourself, and the analytical rigor to stand behind the results.

• Familiarity with SCADA systems and industrial communication protocols such as Modbus, DNP3, CAN, and IEC 61850.

• Comfort on the bench with power supplies, oscilloscopes, transducers, and data acquisition hardware.

• The ability to present technical findings credibly to engineering audiences and clearly to field and commissioning personnel.

Preferred Experience

• Experience with grid-forming and grid-following inverter control.

• Experience with uninterruptible power supply systems, microgrids, or facilities serving critical load.

• Familiarity with ISO or utility interconnection requirements, model quality testing, or third-party product certification.

• Continuous-integration pipelines driving automated test suites, with version control applied to models as rigorously as to code.

• Prior collaboration with national laboratories or university test centers.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Consumer Insights
jobs.description:
Company Overview (Who are we? Why should you join us?)

At ecoATM the proof of our success is in our staggering growth, extraordinary impact on protecting the planet, and providing a work culture unlike any other. We are a technology company and a pioneer of device re-commerce. Through our 7,000 automated kiosks and online marketplace Gazelle.com, we enable people all over the world to join the mobile device re-use revolution, a revolution that will get billions of used smartphones out of the e-waste cycle and into the hands of people who don’t have affordable access to the empowerment of the latest mobile technology.

At ecoATM we know our employees are our greatest strength and the key to our continued growth and success. When you join our team, you will enjoy more than just a job, you will be empowered to develop and utilize your unique talents and skills to build a rewarding career while making a lasting, positive impact on the planet.

Our Values and Leadership Behaviors

Position Summary

The Senior Director, Consumer Insights will lead ecoATM Gazelle's consumer and market insights function, providing a data-driven understanding of customer behavior, motivations, and market trends to inform product, marketing, and business strategy. This role will build a scalable insights capability, spanning quantitative and qualitative research, 1P kiosk transaction and behavioral data, and competitive/market intelligence to provide leadership clear visibility into the customer journey and emerging opportunities. This is a highly visible role during ecoATM Gazelle's post-acquisition growth phase and IPO readiness period, partnering closely with the Executive Management Team (EMT) to ensure strategic investment decisions are grounded in a strong understanding of the consumer.

Key Responsibilities

• Own the end-to-end consumer insights strategy, including synthesizing primary research (surveys, focus groups, interviews), first-party transactional data, behavioral analytics, competitive intelligence, and market trends into actionable recommendations that translate into action across the organization

• Establish an aligned-upon consumer learning agenda that prioritizes the most important strategic questions facing the business

• Establish and manage processes to partner with Marketing, Product, and Business Development to embed consumer insights into go-to-market strategy, product roadmap decisions, and channel/partnership evaluation (e.g., retail embedding, enterprise channels).

• Develop segmentation models and customer journey maps to inform targeting and experience design

• Track competitive landscape and market trends relevant to recommerce, consumer electronics, and adjacent categories

• Present insights and recommendations to the Executive Management Team and board as part of strategic planning and IPO narrative development

• Manage relationships with external research vendors and panels; oversee research budget

• Establish insights reporting cadence and self-service dashboards/tools so stakeholders across the business can access consumer data

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in marketing, Statistics, Psychology, Business, or related field; advanced degree a plus

• 8+ years of consumer/market research or insights experience, with at least 3 years in a leadership role

• Strong quantitative skills, including experience with survey design, segmentation, and statistical analysis

• Experience translating research into clear, actionable business recommendations for senior leadership

• Familiarity with behavioral/transactional data analysis in addition to traditional survey-based research

• Excellent presentation and storytelling skills; comfortable presenting to executive leadership and the board

• Experience in retail, consumer electronics, recommerce, or a fast-paced, PE-backed environment preferred

Success Metrics (First 12 Months)

• Consumer insights meaningfully influence major strategic decisions across product, marketing, and partnerships

• Development of actionable customer segmentation, journey maps, and behavioral frameworks

• Measurable business impact of research-driven recommendations

• Increased effectiveness of product launches, customer experiences, and marketing campaigns informed by consumer insights

• Establishment of a scalable framework that continuously improves the organization's understanding of customers and the market

Travel

<10%

Location (Where will you be working?)

Remote, USA

Pay Range (How much might you earn in your base salary?)

$190,000 - $225,000 (annually)

This position is eligible for short-term and long-term incentives based on individual and company performance.

Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This information is provided per CA SB 1162 (“CA Pay Transparency Law”). Base pay information is based on market location. Learn more about ecoATM benefits here.

This position may also be eligible for short-term and long-term incentives based on individual and company performance.

This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employee may perform other related duties as assigned to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.

jobs.title: Senior IT Site Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world.

AI at SharkNinja

At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

Job Overview

The IT Site Engineer is part of SharkNinja’s Information Technology organization and serves as a critical first line of technology support for our associates. The End User Services team enables SharkNinja’s global workforce by delivering reliable end-user technology, identity and access support, endpoint management, and responsive IT services that keep associates connected and productive.

Reporting to the Director, End User Services, you will resolve technology issues, provision and support hardware and user access, and deliver a consistent, high-quality support experience across our office and remote workforce. You will work collaboratively across IT teams, applying strong technical judgment while identifying opportunities to improve processes and the overall associate experience.

You’ll bring SharkNinja’s Outrageously Extraordinary mindset to your work through Relentless Drive for Edge, continuously looking for smarter ways to improve the support experience, and Insatiable Impatience for Action, moving quickly to diagnose issues, restore service, and keep our teams productive.

Success in this role means being RARELY SATISFIED and embracing PROGRESS OVER PERFECTION—learning from recurring issues, improving processes and documentation, and connecting the dots across systems to continuously strengthen IT support.

Responsibilities

• Serve as a first point of contact for IT incidents and service requests, categorizing, prioritizing, tracking, and resolving tickets against established SLAs in Jira Service Management (JSM).

• Troubleshoot Windows and macOS endpoints, WiFi and network connectivity, and computer performance issues, including slow boot, CPU/RAM utilization, and disk health.

• Create and manage user accounts through Adaxes and Active Directory / Entra ID, including account unlocks, password resets, group membership, and MFA enrollment or reset.

• Administer Microsoft 365 support requests, including mailbox connectivity, missing mail, send-as permissions, quota issues, calendar permissions, distribution lists, and licenses.

• Support the full associate technology lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, and access changes, while maintaining accurate records and following established IT processes.

• Support endpoint provisioning and management using Microsoft Intune, Windows Autopilot, and Jamf across Windows, macOS, and iOS environments.

• Diagnose technology issues efficiently and escalate to Tier 2 or Tier 3 teams when resolution falls outside Tier 1 scope, keeping associates informed throughout the support experience.

• Create and maintain accurate resolution notes, SOPs, runbooks, and self-service documentation in Confluence, recognizing that DETAILS MAKE THE DIFFERENCE.

• Participate as a member of the Major Incident Management team, supporting critical incident triage, technical investigation, service restoration, stakeholder communications, escalation, and post-incident review activities.

• Partner with End User Services and other IT teams to resolve issues, share knowledge, and continuously improve the associate technology experience—because WINNING IS A TEAM SPORT.

• Practice COMMUNICATING FOR IMPACT by providing clear and timely updates, actively listening to associate needs, documenting actions accurately, and translating technical issues into understandable next steps.

• Identify recurring issues and opportunities to improve support processes, documentation, automation, and service quality.

• Demonstrate Deep-Seated Confidence when troubleshooting unfamiliar or ambiguous issues, using sound judgment to determine when additional expertise or escalation is required.

• Bring Genuine Belief in the Journey by embracing evolving technologies, processes, and priorities as SharkNinja’s global technology environment continues to grow.

• Travel up to 10% domestically and internationally as needed to support SharkNinja office locations, technology deployments, training, and business initiatives.

• Provide occasional support outside standard business hours for global technology initiatives, planned changes, critical incidents, and major incident response.

Skills Required

• 3–5 years of IT helpdesk, desktop support, or comparable end-user technology support experience.

• Mac Administration is a MUST: Experience administering and supporting MacBook/macOS environments using Jamf, including device enrollment, configuration, application deployment, security policies, patching, and troubleshooting.

• Experience supporting a Microsoft-focused technology environment, including Windows, Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint), Entra ID, and Intune.

• Working knowledge of Active Directory, Entra ID, and Microsoft 365 Admin Center.

• Familiarity with Microsoft Intune, Windows Autopilot for endpoint provisioning and management.

• Experience with Jira Service Management (JSM) or a comparable ITSM platform, including ticket categorization, SLA tracking, escalation, and resolution documentation.

• Strong troubleshooting skills across endpoint performance, network connectivity, identity and access, email, software, and other common end-user technology issues.

• Experience supporting a geographically distributed or remote workforce is preferred.

• CompTIA A+ or an equivalent technical certification is preferred.

• ITIL 4 Foundation certification is preferred.

• Strong customer-service orientation with the ability to build trust through responsive, professional, and solutions-focused technology support.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to COMMUNICATE FOR IMPACT with both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple requests and shifting priorities while maintaining service quality.

• A RARELY SATISFIED mindset, with the curiosity to understand root causes and continually identify better ways of working.

• A PROGRESS OVER PERFECTION approach that balances thoughtful troubleshooting with the urgency to take action and move issues toward resolution.

• A collaborative mindset grounded in WINNING IS A TEAM SPORT, with the ability to work effectively across IT teams, share knowledge, and escalate when appropriate.

• Ability to work with general guidance, connect information across systems, and apply established IT practices to resolve a variety of support situations.

• Must be eligible to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Salary and Other Compensation: The annual salary range for this position is displayed below. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, flexible spending accounts, health savings accounts (HSA) with company contribution, 401(k) retirement plan with matching, employee stock purchase program, life insurance, AD&D, short-term disability insurance, long-term disability insurance, generous paid time off, company holidays, parental leave, identity theft protection, pet insurance, pre-paid legal insurance, back-up child and eldercare days, product discounts, referral bonus program, and more.

Pay Range

$62,400—$95,700 USD

Our Culture

At SharkNinja, we don’t just raise the bar—we push past it every single day.  Our Outrageously Extraordinary mindset drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home.

What We Offer

We offer competitive health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, employee stock purchase options, wellness programs, SharkNinja product discounts, and more. We empower your personal and professional growth with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community. Together, we won’t just launch products—we’ll disrupt entire markets.

At SharkNinja, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion are vital to our global success. Valuing each unique voice and blending all of our diverse skills strengthens SharkNinja’s innovation every day. We support ALL associates in bringing their authentic selves to work, making an impact, and having the opportunity for career acceleration. With help from our leadership, associates, and our community, we aim to have equity be a key component of the SharkNinja DNA.

Learn more about us:
Life At SharkNinja
Outrageously Extraordinary

jobs.title: Executive Director, Data Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are

VML is a global creative company that combines brand experience, customer experience, and commerce to create connected brands that drive growth. Guided by a Human First philosophy, VML is known for its innovative work for brands and consistently ranks among the world’s leading creative companies, including the WARC Creative 100. VML’s global network spans 55+ markets with principal offices in Buenos Aires, Kansas City, London, New York, São Paulo, Shanghai and Singapore.

VML is part of WPP, the trusted growth partner for the world's leading brands. Powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform WPP Open, WPP unites cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, creativity, production, enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel.

For more information, please visit www.vml.com and follow along on  LinkedIn #WeAreVML.

About the Role

We’re seeking a Executive Director of Data Engineering to lead the architecture, infrastructure, and engineering standards that power our global marketing intelligence capabilities. Reporting directly to the Chief Marketing Intelligence Officer, this leader will modernize our AI infrastructure, accelerate how we build and deliver, and set global data standards across every domain we touch — creative, CX/site, CRM, audience, and media data. The ideal candidate is a hands-on technologist and a strategic leader who can build best-in-class engineering practices at global scale while driving the move toward agile, automated, and AI-native data delivery.

What You’ll Do

AI Infrastructure & Engineering Modernization

• Design and evolve scalable AI and data infrastructure that supports predictive, prescriptive, and generative use cases across the function.

• Establish standards and tooling for accelerated delivery and faster coding — including AI-assisted development, reusable components, and automation that compresses time-to-value.

• Evaluate and introduce new technologies that enable innovation across creative, CX/site, CRM, audience, and media data domains.

• Mature our MLOps and deployment practices so models and data products move from prototype to production reliably and repeatably.

Data Standards, Taxonomies & Governance

• Develop comprehensive, future-proof data taxonomies and data standards that bring consistency and interoperability across domains and regions.

• Set and govern global data standards — architecture, quality, lineage, documentation, and metadata — that scale across the network and agency partners.

• Embed data governance, privacy, and security by design, ensuring compliance with global regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) and responsible AI practices.

• Create a single, trusted foundation for data that improves accuracy, accessibility, and reuse across teams.

Delivery Excellence & AI Integration

• Drive continuous progress toward agile, automated, and effective data delivery, embedding DevOps/DataOps practices and CI/CD across engineering workflows.

• Define and uphold best-in-class standards for AI integration, from data pipelines through model deployment and monitoring.

• Build and lead a high-performing, globally distributed engineering organization, raising the bar on technical excellence, velocity, and reliability.

• Partner with product, analytics, and agency teams to ensure infrastructure and standards translate into faster, higher-quality outcomes.

What You’ll Bring

• 20+ years of experience in data engineering, data architecture, or platform engineering, including senior leadership of global or distributed engineering teams.

• Deep expertise in modern data infrastructure, cloud platforms, and AI/ML engineering, with hands-on command of scalable pipeline and platform design.

• Proven success establishing data taxonomies, standards, and governance frameworks across complex, multi-domain environments.

• Experience modernizing engineering practices toward automation, agile delivery, and AI-assisted development.

• Strong understanding of marketing and media data domains — creative, CX/site, CRM, audience, and media — ideally within automotive, broader industry, or agency/media agency contexts.

• Track record of integrating AI responsibly and at scale, with fluency in MLOps, DataOps, and data governance.

• Exceptional leadership, communication, and stakeholder-management skills at the executive level.

Individual compensation varies based on job-related factors, including location, business needs, level of responsibility, experience, and qualifications. We offer a competitive benefits package, click WPP Benefits for more details.

$155,000—$390,000 USD

That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office an average of four days a week. jobs.title: Senior/Staff User Researcher (U.S. Air Force)
jobs.description:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, user researchers play a critical role in planning, designing, and carrying out research activities with users to help teams gain a deep understanding of the people that use government services. This research informs policy, service, content, and interaction design so that government services work well for users and achieve policy intent.

Skylight has partnered with the U.S. Air Force across multiple legacy modernization efforts. The work spans modernization of legacy systems, new capability development in multi-vendor environments, iteration on established platforms, all inside an agile transformation and broader organizational change.

You’ll own research for a legacy modernization effort: planning studies, finding your way to users inside a large organization where access varies, and turning findings into direction the product and design teams act on. You’ll also help your government partners build their own research muscle.

What to know going in

Your first 30 days are about working with the Skylight team and government personnel, learning the client’s domain and organization, and enabling your government partners. Access to users varies from team to team, so you’ll need to get creative about how you reach them. The client is early- to mid-transformation, so expect organizational and operational change along the way.

This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.

What you’ll do

• Develop research plans (e.g., what methods to use) in alignment with the strategic context of the project

• Find and connect with good user research participants, getting creative about access when direct paths to users aren’t available

• Apply a mix of quantitative and qualitative user research techniques (e.g., user interviews, contextual inquiry) to gain a greater understanding of user needs

• Clearly communicate research findings with internal and external collaborators, and translate them into service/product design hypotheses

• Employ usability testing to validate those hypotheses

• Guide the direction of the service/product and continually advocate for users

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

• Ability to align user research activities with organizational strategy and objectives

• Can correctly apply a wide-range of user research methods at different stages of the product life cycle

• Understand how to include all kinds of users in appropriate research activities to help teams deliver accessible services

• Can turn research data into clear findings that inform decisions

• Ability to help colleagues better understand the social and technological context for government services (e.g., how digital technology is changing user behavior)

• Possess an understanding of the different technologies and technical roles within a multidisciplinary team used to build and operate digital services

• Can apply user-centered design practices within the context of an agile, multidisciplinary team

• Interest in mentoring, coaching, and pairing with government partners so they can carry the work forward

• Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery

• A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

• Military or government experience

• Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings

• A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

• Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.

• All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.

• This contract requires U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment.

• You must be able to obtain and maintain a Common Access Card (CAC), which requires a favorable background check.

• You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

Expect occasional travel to Air Force bases across the U.S., quarterly at most.

Expected start date

November 2026

Care package

Salary

We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a User Researcher at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows:

• Associate User Researcher: $90,000–$125,000

• User Researcher I: $120,000–$140,000

• User Researcher II: $135,000–$160,000

• Senior User Researcher: $150,000–$185,000

• Staff User Researcher: $170,000–$203,000

• Principal User Researcher: $180,000–$230,000

Benefits

Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways:

• Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance

• Short-term and long-term disability insurance

• Life and AD&D insurance

• Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account

• Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period

• Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays

• Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents

• Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options

• Business development / sales bonuses

• Referral bonuses

• Annual $2000 allowance for professional development

• Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases

• Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more)

• Flexible, remote-friendly work environment

• An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good

Interview tips

Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview:

• Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works.

• Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them.

• Browse our case studies to learn more about our work.

If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital.

We participate in E-Verify and upon hire, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you’re authorized to work in the U.S.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable law.
